starting_principles: Definition of moment of inertia of a continuous body: I = int r_perp^2 dm
Euclidean distance in Cartesian coordinate system: r^2 = x^2 + y^2 for points in xy-plane
assumptions: The rigid body is strictly two-dimensional and planar (laminar body)
The body lies entirely in the xy-plane such that z = 0 for every differential mass element dm
The x, y, and z axes are mutually perpendicular and intersect at a common origin O
The z-axis is perpendicular to the plane of the lamina

ordered_steps.description: Establish coordinate frame and express position of mass element
ordered_steps.operation: Identify Cartesian coordinates of differential mass element dm in the lamina plane
assumptions_applied: Planar lamina lying entirely in xy-plane

ordered_steps.description: Formulate moments of inertia about the coplanar x and y axes
ordered_steps.operation: Determine perpendicular distance to x-axis (|y|) and y-axis (|x|)
ordered_steps.result_equation: I_x = \int y^2 \, dm, \quad I_y = \int x^2 \, dm
assumptions_applied: Perpendicular distance from x-axis is y, from y-axis is x

ordered_steps.description: Formulate moment of inertia about perpendicular z-axis through origin
ordered_steps.operation: Express perpendicular distance r_z from z-axis using Pythagorean theorem in xy plane
ordered_steps.result_equation: r_z^2 = x^2 + y^2 \implies I_z = \int (x^2 + y^2) \, dm
assumptions_applied: Origin O is common intersection of all three axes

ordered_steps.description: Distribute integral by linearity and substitute coplanar definitions
ordered_steps.operation: Apply linearity of integration: int (x^2 + y^2) dm = int x^2 dm + int y^2 dm
ordered_steps.result_equation: I_z = \int x^2 \, dm + \int y^2 \, dm = I_y + I_x

ordered_steps.description: Conclude perpendicular axis theorem and state dimensional equivalence

applicability_conditions: Strictly restricted to two-dimensional planar laminas
Fails identically for any 3D body with non-zero z-thickness because r_x^2 = y^2 + z^2 and r_y^2 = x^2 + z^2 lead to I_x + I_y = I_z + 2 int z^2 dm != I_z
source_references: H.C. Verma Vol 1, Chapter 10, Section 10.6 (Theorems of Moment of Inertia)
